title: Fraction and percent word problems
blurb: Solve one- and two-step fraction and percent word problems: decide what each fraction or percent is taken of, and answer the exact question asked.
question: A 750 mL IV bag is hung. The nurse infuses 2/5 of it before noon, then 1/3 of what remains during the afternoon. How much is left in the bag, and why is 450 mL a trap?

teach.h: Word problems are reading problems first
teach.body: Formally, a fraction or percent word problem describes a situation in which a fraction or percent is applied to a base amount, often in two steps. In plain English: most wrong answers on HESI A2 word problems are not arithmetic mistakes. They come from taking the fraction of the wrong amount, or from stopping one step early. The options are built from exactly those numbers, so a fixed routine protects you.

teach.h: Of the whole, or of the rest?
teach.body: Every fraction or percent is taken OF something. "1/3 of the bag" or "20% of the budget" means the original whole. "1/3 of what remains" or "20% of the rest" means the amount left after the earlier step. Two percents of the same whole can be added (12% + 8% = 20% of the pay); a percent of the rest cannot. "Of" means multiply: 3/5 of 40 = 40 ÷ 5 × 3 = 24, and 35% of 80 = 0.35 × 80 = 28.

items: Question: how much is LEFT in the 750 mL bag at the end?
Before noon: 2/5 of 750 = 750 ÷ 5 × 2 = 300 mL used. Left: 750 − 300 = 450 mL.
Afternoon: 1/3 of the REMAINDER (450, not 750) = 150 mL used. Left: 450 − 150 = 300 mL.
Options you would see: 450 mL (left at noon, one step early) and 200 mL (the afternoon 1/3 taken from the full 750 instead of the 450 remaining).

teach.h: The IV bag, step by step
Worked example: a percent, then a fraction
items: A unit has 80 patients. 35% are on a fluid restriction, and 3/4 of those also have a daily weight ordered. How many have both?
Fluid restriction: 0.35 × 80 = 28 patients. Check: 10% is 8, so 30% is 24 and 5% is 4; 24 + 4 = 28. ✓
Traps: 28 (one step early), 60 (3/4 of all 80) and 7 (the restricted patients without a daily weight).

teach.text: The costliest slips: taking the second fraction or percent of the original whole instead of the remainder; adding a percent of the rest to a percent of the whole (40% then 25% of the rest is not 65% off); stopping one step early; and answering "how much is left" with the amount used.

teach.h: The fraction or percent is taken of...

teach.body: Jamal Brooks, a nursing applicant, takes home $1,840 a month. Rent is $725, his car costs $260 and groceries $310, and he saves 15% of his take-home pay. Savings: 0.15 × 1,840 = $276 (10% is 184, 5% is 92). Out: 725 + 260 + 310 + 276 = $1,571. Left: 1,840 − 1,571 = $269. The 15% is of his take-home pay, not of what is left after bills, so it comes from the full $1,840.

items: Read the last line first: left, used, total or how many more.
Find the base of every fraction and percent: the whole, or what remains.
Percents of the same whole add; a percent of the rest must be done as a second step.
To find a whole from a part, divide the part by its fraction or percent.
Check the answer against the question; intermediate values are the distractors.

summary: You can now solve one- and two-step fraction and percent word problems by finding the base of each fraction or percent (the whole or what remains), working one step at a time, and answering the exact question asked. You recognize the one-step-early, wrong-base and added-percent options the HESI A2 sets.

A.q: A 1,200 mL bag is hung. In the morning, 3/8 of it is infused. In the afternoon, 1/2 of what remains is infused. How much is left in the bag?
A.why: Morning: 3/8 × 1,200 = 450 mL used, leaving 750. Afternoon: 1/2 × 750 = 375 used, leaving 375 mL. Check: 450 + 375 + 375 = 1,200. ✓

whyNot.0: 750 mL is what was left after the morning, one step early.
whyNot.1: 150 mL takes the afternoon half from the full 1,200 instead of from the remainder.
whyNot.2: 825 mL is the total infused (450 + 375), not the amount left.

A.q: In a class of 36 nursing students, 2/3 passed the first exam. Of those who passed, 3/4 earned a B or higher. How many students earned a B or higher?

whyNot.0: 27 takes 3/4 of all 36 students instead of 3/4 of the 24 who passed.
whyNot.2: 24 is the number who passed, one step short of the answer.
whyNot.3: 6 is the number who passed with less than a B (24 − 18).

A.q: A hospital has 450 beds, and 84% of them are occupied. How many beds are empty?

whyNot.1: 378 is the number of occupied beds, not empty ones.
whyNot.2: 366 subtracts 84 beds from 450; 84 is a percent, not a number of beds.
whyNot.3: 45 rounds 84% up to 90% and takes the 10% left; the exact share empty is 16%.

B.q: A patient's fluid restriction is 2,000 mL a day. She drinks 3/8 of it at breakfast and 1/5 of the full amount at lunch. How many milliliters are left?
B.why: Breakfast: 3/8 × 2,000 = 750 mL. Lunch: 1/5 × 2,000 = 400 mL (of the FULL amount). Left: 2,000 − 750 − 400 = 850 mL.

whyNot.0: 1,250 mL is what was left after breakfast, one step early.
whyNot.1: 1,000 mL takes 1/5 of the 1,250 mL remaining; the stem says 1/5 of the full amount.
whyNot.3: 1,150 mL is the total she drank (750 + 400), not the amount left.

B.q: A student has a $360 textbook budget. She spends 45% of it on one book, then 1/3 of the remaining money on another. How much of the budget is left?
B.why: First book: 0.45 × 360 = $162, leaving $198. Second book: 1/3 × 198 = $66, leaving 198 − 66 = $132.

whyNot.0: $198 is what was left after the first book, one step early.
whyNot.1: $66 is the cost of the second book, not the amount left.
whyNot.3: $78 takes 1/3 of the full $360 ($120) instead of 1/3 of the $198 remaining.

B.q: After using 5/8 of a box of exam gloves, a nurse has 60 gloves left. How many gloves were in the full box?

whyNot.0: 96 divides 60 by 5/8, treating the 60 left as the part used.
whyNot.1: 120 treats the 60 gloves left as half of the box.
whyNot.2: 480 treats the 60 gloves as 1/8 of the box instead of 3/8 (60 × 8).

C.q: A nursing student must complete 120 clinical hours. She completes 40% of them in March and 5/12 of the remaining hours in April. How many hours remain after April?
C.why: March: 0.40 × 120 = 48 hours, leaving 72. April: 5/12 × 72 = 30 hours, leaving 72 − 30 = 42 hours.

whyNot.1: 72 hours is what remained after March, one step early.
whyNot.2: 30 is the number of hours completed in April, not the hours remaining.
whyNot.3: 22 takes 5/12 of the full 120 hours (50) instead of 5/12 of the 72 remaining.

C.q: Jada earns $19.50 an hour and works 36 hours a week. Her employer withholds 20% of her pay. She spends $310 a week. How much does she have left to save each week?

whyNot.0: $392.00 subtracts spending from gross pay and forgets the 20% withholding.
whyNot.1: $313.60 takes 20% off after subtracting spending; withholding comes out of the full paycheck.
whyNot.3: $140.40 is the amount withheld (20% of 702), not the amount left.

C.q: Of 300 patients surveyed, 3/5 rated their care as excellent. Of the rest, 25% rated it as poor. How many patients rated their care as poor?

whyNot.0: 75 takes 25% of all 300 patients instead of 25% of the 120 who did not rate care excellent.
whyNot.1: 45 takes 25% of the 180 who rated care excellent instead of the rest.
whyNot.2: 90 is the rest who did not rate care as poor (120 − 30).

reteach.title: A GPS for word problems
reteach.question: A GPS asks for your destination before it plans the route. What happens if you start driving before you know where you are going, and how does that match a word problem?

blocks.body: A GPS never starts with the first turn; it starts with the destination. In a word problem the destination is the question's last line: "how much is LEFT", "how many MORE", "how many in ALL". Each calculation is a turn along the route, and each turn starts from where the last one ended: "1/3 of what remains" starts from the remainder, not from home. The distractors are the places you pass on the way.

blocks.h: The IV bag route: destination 'how much is left'

steps.sub: 450 left: a stop, not the end

blocks.text: If your answer appears among the options after only one step of a two-step problem, be suspicious. Reread the last line before you choose.

explain.body: Do the first step, subtract to find what remains, then take the second fraction of that remainder. 900 mL: 2/5 used is 360, leaving 540; 1/4 of 540 is 135, leaving 405.

test.q: A 900 mL bottle of tube feeding is opened. A patient receives 2/5 of it in the morning and 1/4 of the remainder at noon. How many milliliters are left?

whyNot.0: 540 is what was left after the morning, one step early.
whyNot.1: 315 takes 1/4 of the full 900 (225) instead of 1/4 of the 540 remaining.
whyNot.2: 135 is the amount given at noon, not the amount left.

explain.body: When the question asks about the other group, subtract the percent from 100% first, or find the part and subtract it from the total. 12% referred means 88% not referred.

test.q: A clinic saw 250 patients, and 12% were referred to a specialist. How many patients were not referred?

whyNot.0: 30 is the number referred, not the number not referred.
whyNot.2: 238 subtracts 12 patients from 250; 12 is a percent, not a number of patients.
whyNot.3: 225 rounds 12% down to 10% (25 patients) before subtracting.

explain.h: Finding the whole from a part
explain.body: If 2/3 is used and 50 mL remain, the 50 mL is the other 1/3. Divide the part by its fraction: 50 ÷ 1/3 = 150 mL.

test.q: After 2/3 of a bottle of cough syrup is used, 50 mL remain. How many milliliters did the full bottle hold?
test.why: 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 remains. 50 mL is 1/3 of the bottle, so the bottle held 50 ÷ 1/3 = 150 mL. Check: 1/3 × 150 = 50.

whyNot.0: 75 mL divides 50 by 2/3, treating the 50 mL left as the part used.
whyNot.1: 100 mL treats the 50 mL left as half of the bottle.
whyNot.3: 33 1/3 mL takes 2/3 of the 50 mL instead of finding the whole.

explain.h: A fraction, then a percent of the rest
explain.body: Mixed problems use both forms: take the fraction, find the rest, then take the percent of the rest. 1/4 of $480 is $120, leaving $360; 30% of $360 is $108.

test.q: Of a $480 paycheck, 1/4 goes to rent and 30% of the rest goes to groceries. How much goes to groceries?

whyNot.0: $144 takes 30% of the full $480 instead of 30% of the $360 left after rent.
whyNot.2: $360 is the money left after rent, one step short of the answer.
whyNot.3: $252 is the money left after rent and groceries (360 − 108), not the grocery amount.
